summary: Build 1 of the microlensing program: a new `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/` subpackage (geometry / contour-free operator / topology-stable channels) restructured from the research prototype in `.claude/spec/lensing_paper/code/`, with oracle, exact-reconstruction, continuity and performance tests. Two consultations reshaped the brief materially. (1) PROFESSOR — DECISIVE: the operator has two compounding cancellation channels, seed Maclaurin ~e^{w|y'|} and operator series ~e^{gamma'*w/2}, giving loss law rel_err ~ eps*e^L/(sqrt(pi*w)*|y'|) with L = w(|y'| + gamma'/2). The law was calibrated twice against the paper's own numbers (its reported 9.4e-11 worst-case continuation error = e^{gamma'w/2}*eps at gamma'~0.6,w=40; and its need for 60-80 dps). Plain double tops out at L<=12-15, but the paper's OWN headline config (kappa=gamma=0.2, y=0.55, w=40) sits at L=29.6 — a plain-double kernel returns ~2e-4, not the brief's mandated 1e-10, and cannot reproduce the paper's figures. The build therefore requires hand-rolled DOUBLE-DOUBLE internal accumulation (complex128 in/out; Dekker TwoSum/TwoProduct; dd-complex as 4 float64 scalars), certified to L<=48. This is the single largest scope change vs the brief and the Simplifier independently endorsed it as justified (rejecting both a deferral to Build 2 and an L<=12 domain cap, on the grounds that a gerrymandered domain is an incomplete deliverable wearing a passing test suite). (2) The brief's tolerance requirements 1b (reconstruction 1e-12) and 1d (mass-sheet 1e-13) are ALGEBRAIC TAUTOLOGIES — F_op appears on both sides of the reconstruction identity, and the prototype's shipped mass-sheet test passes identical series arguments to both sides, so its 2e-12 threshold is theater. Both are re-phrased as internal-consistency tests, with the reconstruction tolerance normalized by max(|F_op|, sum|K_a|, max_a|H_a|) rather than by |F_op|, because |H_a| ~ lambda_soft^{-6.5} near critical curves. Real accuracy is gated by T3 (F_op vs mpmath oracle) and T4 (geometric-optics w^-3 convergence — the strongest test available, coupling operator+prefactor+quartic+magnifications+Morse indices+C1/C2 through a channel with no shared code). (3) SIMPLIFIER cut ~450 lines the brief implied porting: `chang_refsdal_exact_partition.py` is superseded (no test imports it), which dissolves the '9-dataclass sprawl' for free; and `build_fold_crossing_partition`/`build_cusp_crossing_partition` (~330 L, 2 dataclasses) are validated-but-unused surface never called by `GlobalChannelTracker.evaluate()` — the fold/cusp continuity requirement is met instead by driving the general tracker along crossing paths, exactly as the prototype's own path test already does. Four further cuts (no large-|z| asymptotic branch, no k-recurrence, no exp() in the seed via closed-form |C(w)|, beta rotated to the shear eigenframe) are net simplifications AND correctness fixes. ASSUMPTIONS DOCUMENTED: (a) mpmath becomes a `test` extra with NO skipUnless guard — a skip on the build gate would let the top correctness test silently vanish exactly where it should fail loud, following the repo's fail-loud pymultinest precedent; (b) I overruled the Simplifier on the `branch` ('wave'|'geometric') gate — it conflated it with the cut asymptotic-1F1 branch, but it is a distinct global gate that skips F_op entirely in geometric optics, needed because in-band w reaches 127+ (beyond the L<=48 wave ceiling) and demanded by brief req 2; note the brief is technically WRONG that the switch machinery achieves this, since G_C = F_op - sum_p e^{iw*tau_p} H_p calls F_op at every frequency; (c) I overruled the Simplifier's dd-seed-only fallback in favour of dd throughout, since gamma'=0.9 at w=40 gives gamma'w/2=18 > the fallback's limit of 8, and gamma'->1 is the astrophysically interesting high-magnification limit; perf headroom is 10-200x. MEMORY CHECKPOINT BLOCKED: `mcp__serena__edit_memory` is non-read-only and plan mode refused it (same blocker as the prior cw_prof_prompt entry). The full checkpoint text is carried in this summary and its persistence is assigned to WP7.

work_packages.title: Subpackage skeleton + geometry.py port
work_packages.what: Create the `cogwheel/lensing/` and `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/` package skeleton and port the prototype's pure-numpy lens geometry: macro matrix, quartic image solver, delays/Hessians/signed magnifications/Morse indices, stationary-phase C1/C2 coefficients, image kernels, and critical-curve / nearest-caustic utilities. Add the `test` extra to pyproject. This WP is a LEAF — it has no dependency on the operator or the hypergeometric kernel and must be scheduled in parallel with WP2/WP3.
where: NEW: `cogwheel/lensing/__init__.py`, `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/__init__.py`, `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/geometry.py`, `cogwheel/tests/test_lensing_geometry.py`. EDIT: `pyproject.toml`. SOURCE: `.claude/spec/lensing_paper/code/chang_refsdal_geometry.py` (~330 L, pure numpy, leaf); paper Appendices A and B.
work_packages.how: Port `macro_matrix`, `hessian`, `lens_residual`, `delay`, `image_quartic_coefficients`, `find_images_quartic`, `find_images`, `saddle_coefficients`, `image_kernel`, `critical_point`, plus the `nearest_caustic_point` helper currently living in `chang_refsdal_global_tracking.py` (it is geometry, not tracking — move it here). Keep the private `_source_frame`, `_newton_polish`, `_centered_source_images` structure. CRITICAL DIRECTIVES: (1) `np.roots` is NOT numba-compatible and geometry is ~0.5% of runtime (the paper states image finding is negligible next to special-function evaluation) — leave geometry in plain numpy; the njit boundary is WP2/WP3 only. (2) `np.roots` gives only ~sqrt(eps)~1e-8 accuracy near a double root, i.e. near every caustic, which is where we operate; the Newton polish is mandatory but its Jacobian is SINGULAR there so the polish stalls — the prototype's fallback (keep the algebraic candidate when Newton makes the residual worse) is LOAD-BEARING, do not 'clean it up'. (3) Consequence: near-caustic positions are ~1e-8 but delays are ~1e-16 (since grad tau = 0, position error enters tau quadratically) — assert on delays and residuals, never on positions, near caustics. (4) The quartic reconstruction x'_1 = Y(d-u)/D has a removable singularity at b=0 (source on a shear axis) and the prototype's `axis_tolerance=5e-11` is a knife edge — a source at beta+1e-9 takes the generic branch with D(u)~0. PREFER recovering x' from the null space of (A' - u*I) when |D(u)| is small over two hard-coded branches. (5) Enforce 1-kappa > |gamma| strictly with a named exception; raise on gamma=0 AND y=0 (Einstein ring) and on x=0 (the -ln|x| singularity). (6) C1 ~ lambda_soft^-3 and C2 ~ lambda_soft^-6 near critical curves, so H_a ~ lambda_soft^-6.5 — this divergence is arithmetic, not a bug; expose max_a|H_a| so WP6's reconstruction test can normalize by it. Units/conventions: angles in point-mass Einstein-radius units, w dimensionless. Module docstring states WHAT/WHY per cogwheel idiom, numpy-style API docs, pylint max-line-length=79. `cogwheel/lensing/__init__.py` carries the docstring (follow `cogwheel/likelihood/__init__.py`); the nested `__init__.py` may be bare (follow `likelihood/marginalization/__init__.py`). Do NOT add `from . import lensing` to `cogwheel/__init__.py` — it imports no submodules by design. Both `__init__.py` files are REQUIRED for packaging (`namespaces = false` means a missing one silently drops the package from the wheel); no `packages=[...]` edit is needed. Add `[project.optional-dependencies] test = ["mpmath"]` to pyproject — mpmath is oracle-only and must NEVER be imported by production code. No DATA_CONTRACTS.yaml change (no new disk artifacts).
work_packages.verification: `python -m unittest cogwheel.tests.test_lensing_geometry` passes. Implements domain tests T8a (quartic vs the shipped 168-row validation CSV: n_quartic == n_multistart in 168/168, max residual <= 1e-12, matched position error <= 3e-12) and the ported prototype assertions (random-draw quartic residual < 1e-9 over 30 draws; centered-source 4 images at residual < 1e-12). Confirm `import cogwheel.lensing.chang_refsdal.geometry` works and that `pip install -e .` still discovers the new package.

work_packages.title: Double-double arithmetic primitives (_dd.py)
work_packages.what: Implement hand-rolled double-double (two-double) complex arithmetic primitives — the numerical foundation the whole operator rests on. Split out as its own gated WP because a dd bug is SILENT and would otherwise be misdiagnosed as a 1F1 bug, burning a Coder's whole budget on 'is this the primitives or the series?'.
where: NEW: `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/_dd.py` (~150 L), `cogwheel/tests/test_lensing_dd.py`. LEAF module — no dependencies.
work_packages.how: WHY THIS EXISTS (put it in the module docstring): the Chang-Refsdal operator loses ~0.434*L digits with L = w(|y'| + gamma'/2); at the paper's headline config L=29.6, so plain double (eps 2.2e-16, ceiling L~12-15) returns ~2e-4 relative error. dd (eps ~1.2e-32) lifts the ceiling to L~48-52. mpmath is ~1e6x too slow for a likelihood loop. Implement Dekker TwoSum and TwoProduct with splitting constant 2^27+1 = 134217729.0 — numba has NO reliable FMA intrinsic, so use the split, NOT math.fma. DIRECTIVE ON REPRESENTATION: a dd-complex is FOUR SEPARATE float64 scalars (re_hi, re_lo, im_hi, im_lo) passed and returned individually — never a tuple-of-tuples, never a dataclass, never an object array. This is what keeps it numba-compatible (plain loops/scalars/arrays, no object mode). Provide the minimal op set the ladder and operator sum actually need: dd_add, dd_mul, dd_div, dd_complex_add, dd_complex_mul, dd_complex_div, and conversion to/from complex128. YAGNI: do NOT implement dd sqrt/exp/log/trig — nothing in the hot path needs them (the prefactor is computed once in plain double via the closed form in WP4). Write `@njit`-shaped code but leave the decorator DEFERRED per the brief; document the intended hot path in the docstring. Reference: Dekker 1971; Hida-Li-Bailey (QD library). Keep functions small and single-purpose; pylint 79 cols.
work_packages.verification: `python -m unittest cogwheel.tests.test_lensing_dd` passes. Implements domain test T0: each primitive compared DIRECTLY against mpmath at dps=60 on adversarial inputs (catastrophic cancellation pairs a-b with a~b, products of values spanning many exponents, values near the double overflow/underflow rails), asserting dd relative error <= 1e-30 where mpmath says the answer is representable. The Professor's explicit warning: this is where a Coder silently gets it wrong — the tests must be able to FAIL (verify by temporarily perturbing the splitting constant and confirming the suite goes red).

work_packages.title: Double-precision complex 1F1 kernel (_hypergeometric.py)
work_packages.what: Replace the prototype's sole mpmath call site (`point_mass_G_derivatives`, dps=60-80) with a fast dd-accumulated complex confluent-hypergeometric kernel producing the k-ladder of point-mass seed derivatives. This is the build's highest-risk numerics.
where: NEW: `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/_hypergeometric.py`, `cogwheel/tests/test_lensing_hypergeometric.py`. SOURCE: `.claude/spec/lensing_paper/code/chang_refsdal_operator.py::point_mass_G_derivatives` (the ONLY mpmath user in the prototype); paper Sec. II.B + Appendix C.
work_packages.how: REPARAMETRIZE FIRST — do not implement the paper's literal G form. Apply Kummer once, globally: 1F1(1 - iw/2 + k; 1+k; -iws/2) = e^{-iws/2} * 1F1(iw/2; 1+k; +iws/2), which holds because b_k - a_k = (1+k) - (1+k-iw/2) = iw/2 EXACTLY AND INDEPENDENTLY OF k. Every G^(k) then carries the same e^{-iws/2}, which cancels identically against the final e^{+iws/2}. RESULT: no exp() of an imaginary argument appears anywhere in the seed — the prototype's `pref = e^{pi w/4 + ...}` and its later `phase_scaled = exp(0.5j*w*s')` are BOTH deleted. Define M_k := 1F1(iw/2; 1+k; z'), z' = +i*w*s/2, s=|y'|^2. Three wins: a' = iw/2 is k-independent (one shared numerator sequence); |a'| = w/2 <= |a_k| = sqrt((1+k)^2 + w^2/4) for every k (strictly smaller terms, strictly less cancellation — at k=88, w=40 the per-term modulus ratio is ~2.5, which compounded over ~40 terms is the difference between working and not); and note the classical Kummer motivation (|e^z| shrinkage) is VOID here since z is purely imaginary — this is about k-independence and |a|, not about |e^z|. PREFACTOR — closed form, derived and verified: |Gamma(1-iw/2)|^2 = (pi*w/2)/sinh(pi*w/2), so |C(w)|^2 = e^{pi w/2} * (pi w/2)/sinh(pi w/2) = pi*w/(1 - e^{-pi*w}) EXACTLY for all w>0. The e^{pi w/4} and the e^{-pi w/4} inside |Gamma| cancel identically — overflow risk is gone permanently, not by luck. Implement: mag = sqrt(pi*w / (-expm1(-pi*w))) — expm1 is MANDATORY, since w=0.025 is physical (M_Lz=10 at 20 Hz) and naive 1-exp(-pi*w) loses 2 digits; phase = 0.5*w*log(0.5*w) + imag(scipy.special.loggamma(1 - 0.5j*w)); C = mag*(cos(phase) + 1j*sin(phase)). Do NOT use exp(loggamma(...) + pi*w/4 + ...): it numerically cancels Re loggamma ~ -pi w/4 against +pi w/4 at a cost of ~(pi w/4)*eps. Note the residual floor: arg C carries ~(w/2)ln(w/2)*eps ~ 1.3e-14 rad at w=40, so no ABSOLUTE test of F_op beats ~1e-14 at w=40 regardless of dd (it cancels in ratio tests). LADDER — NO k-RECURRENCE: forward recursion in b=1+k is UNSTABLE because M(a;b;z) -> 1 as b -> inf is the MINIMAL (recessive) solution of DLMF 13.3.3, so upward recursion contaminates it with the dominant ~k!/z^k solution and loses everything by k~|z|; backward Miller is the stable direction but needs a normalization anchor, divides by z (blows up as y->0, exactly where we live near-cusp/near-axis), and its dominance is only asymptotic in k. DIRECTIVE: compute t_m = (iw/2)_m * z'^m / m! ONCE by a recurrence in m (in dd), then M_k = sum_m t_m/(1+k)_m per k — (1+k)_m is real, positive and increasing so it adds NO cancellation. Per k, run g <- g*(iw/2 + m)*z'/((1+k+m)(m+1)) in dd. Cost ~K_max*m_max ~ 7e3 FMAs. NEVER form (1+k)_m via factorials (150! ~ 5.7e262). K_max must reach ~120 (= 2*n_max with n_max adaptive to ~60 at gamma'->0.9), NOT the prototype's 2*36=72. NO LARGE-|z| ASYMPTOTIC BRANCH — DO NOT WRITE IT: the Poincare expansion needs |z| >> |a|^2/|b|, i.e. |y'| >> sqrt(w/2) ~ 4.5 at w=40, where the secondary image has mu ~ y^-4 ~ 2e-3 and there is no measurable lensing signature at any realistic SNR; the regime is physically unreachable. The regime that DOES break the series is large |a| at fixed z/a (the uniform Olver/Airy regime), which is a research project, not Build 1 — the correct large-parameter branch is the stationary-phase H_a kernels (WP6). Use dd accumulation throughout (WP2 primitives). Keep numba-shaped (plain loops/arrays, no object mode), @njit deferred, hot path documented. PRODUCTION MUST NOT IMPORT mpmath.
work_packages.verification: `python -m unittest cogwheel.tests.test_lensing_hypergeometric` passes. Implements domain tests T1 (prefactor / Deguchi-Watson exact identity, rtol <= 1e-14 and FLAT in w) and T2 (ladder vs mpmath oracle + calibration of the loss law: rtol <= 1e-12 wherever w|y'| <= 45; rtol monotonically non-increasing in k; fitted slope of log10(rtol) vs w|y'| = 0.434 +/- 0.05 with intercept consistent with log10(eps_dd) ~ -32 +/- 1; Miller backward recurrence cross-check agrees to 1e-12 for |z'| >= 5, TEST-ONLY). Structural assertion: the production module namespace contains no reference to mpmath.

work_packages.title: Contour-free amplification operator (operator.py)
work_packages.what: Port the contour-free amplification F_op(w, y; gamma, beta, kappa): point-mass seed + D_beta^n source-derivative operator series + EXACT mass-sheet rescaling for kappa. Consumes WP3's kernel. This module is a LEAF w.r.t. geometry (the prototype's operator does not import geometry) and can run in parallel with WP1.
where: NEW: `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/operator.py`, `cogwheel/tests/test_lensing_operator.py`. SOURCE: `.claude/spec/lensing_paper/code/chang_refsdal_operator.py` (~230 L); paper Sec. II.B, Appendix C.
work_packages.how: KEEP the prototype's D_beta^n representation-building (monomials in z, zbar, radial-derivative order) — the brief and both consultations agree it is the clean part. Shear via the operator identity G_gamma = exp[(i*gamma'/(2w)) D_beta] G_PM, adaptively truncated; kappa via the EXACT mass-sheet rescaling F_{kappa,gamma}(w,y;beta) = (1/lambda) * exp[iw(ln(lambda)/2 - kappa|y|^2/(2 lambda))] * F_{0,gamma/lambda}(w, y/sqrt(lambda)), lambda = 1-kappa — purely algebraic, same w, written ONCE. TWO STRUCTURAL WINS THE PROTOTYPE MISSES: (1) ROTATE BETA AWAY. The point mass is circular, so only the source angle relative to the shear axes matters — always rotate to the shear eigenframe (beta == 0) internally, evaluate, rotate back. Then D_0 = 2(d_z^2 + d_zbar^2), the representation coefficients are REAL, and there is exactly ONE cached representation table for all beta. The prototype's `@lru_cache(maxsize=32)` keyed on a continuous `beta_key` is a LIVE PERFORMANCE BUG: beta is continuous, so the cache essentially never hits along a PE path and every miss rebuilds the whole D^n tower. (2) EXPLOIT AND ASSERT THE GRADING. At order n: k = (a+b+2n)/2, n <= k <= 2n, a-b in {2n, 2n-4, ..., -2n}, ~ (n+1)^2/2 keys. k is DETERMINED by (a,b) — store the representation as a dense REAL 2-D array, not a dict, and assert k == (a+b+2n)//2 as a free structural test. k >= n is what makes the series converge as w->0 despite the (i gamma'/(2w))^n coefficient: the worst term is (gamma' w/8)^n/n!. Accumulate the operator sum in dd (WP2) — RULING: dd for BOTH channels, not the seed-only fallback, because gamma'=0.9 at w=40 gives gamma'w/2=18, well past the fallback's limit of 8, and gamma'->1 is the astrophysically INTERESTING limit (mu_macro=30 => gamma'=0.93); perf headroom is 10-200x under the 10 ms budget. Adaptive n_max ~ zeta + 5*sqrt(zeta) + 10 with zeta = gamma'*w/2 (~49 at gamma'=0.9, w=40) — the prototype's max_order=36 is insufficient at gamma' >~ 0.6. RUNTIME REFUSAL, NOT A PASSIVE FLAG: the prototype returns a value when converged=False, which in a sampler is a silent wrong answer the sampler will happily converge on. Compute the MEASURED max_partial_term/|total| (free — you already have the terms) and RAISE a named exception (or return NaN only when diagnostics are explicitly requested) when it exceeds ~1e13; this empirical check supersedes the analytic L bound. DIAGNOSTICS — adjudicated set, do not expand: keep operator_order_used, operator_converged, estimated_relative_tail (the prototype's OperatorDiagnostics is the right shape — do NOT build a second parallel reporting API on top of it) plus the measured max_partial_term/|total|. CUT loss_exponent, predicted_digits_lost, max_kernel_abs (a one-line np.max the caller can do). MODULE DOCSTRING MUST STATE IN BOLD: F includes sqrt(mu_macro) — F_{kappa,gamma}(w->0) -> 1/sqrt((1-kappa)^2 - gamma^2), NOT 1 — or Build 2 will double-count the macro magnification. Also document: 1-kappa > |gamma| enforced strictly with a clear named error; macro saddles (Type II, ~half of astrophysically interesting high-mu images) are OUT OF SCOPE — a documented LIMITATION, not a TODO. Certified domain, stated as the L constraint NOT as a box (a box would be either uselessly small or a lie): L = w(|y'| + gamma'/2) <= 48 with y' = y/sqrt(1-kappa), gamma' = gamma/(1-kappa); w in [1e-3, 300]; |y'| <= 3; gamma' <= 0.9; kappa in [0, 0.6]. Document that the gamma'->1, w >~ 50 corner is NOT reachable in dd and is handed to the stationary-phase branch.
work_packages.verification: `python -m unittest cogwheel.tests.test_lensing_operator` passes. Implements domain tests T3 (F_op vs mpmath oracle over the paper's 4 configurations + oriented-shear + high-reduced-shear stress cases, rtol <= 1e-10 for every point with L <= 48), T6a/T6c/T6d (mass-sheet, in its non-vacuous forms), and the performance assertions (single F_op <= 2 ms at w=20 after warm-up, target <= 200 us, against the brief's 10 ms bound; operator_order_used <= 25 at gamma'=0.25, w=40 to catch adaptive truncation silently running to max_order). Structural assertion: `mpmath` absent from the production import graph — timing alone will not catch a 10-node mpmath path on a fast machine.

work_packages.title: Channel algebra core (_channel_algebra.py)
work_packages.what: Port the prototype's pure-numpy algebraic channel core: the smootherstep switch, the exact cluster kernel, unresolved-member/transition channels, and the residual-projection reconstruction. Split out as its own leaf module (Simplifier's call) because it has ZERO dependency on geometry or the operator and is testable purely as algebraic identities — burying it inside channels.py would trap it behind WP1+WP4 for no benefit.
where: NEW: `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/_channel_algebra.py`, tests folded into `cogwheel/tests/test_lensing_channels.py`. SOURCE: `.claude/spec/lensing_paper/code/exact_gauge_partition.py` (~120 L, leaf, consumed by both topology_stable and global_tracking).
work_packages.how: Port `smootherstep(x, x0, x1)` (the C2 switch), `exact_cluster_kernel`, `unresolved_member_channels`, `exact_transition_channels`, `reconstructed_total`. Keep it pure-numpy and pure-function — no geometry import, no operator import, no scipy. The exact residual projection is K_a = K_hat_a + alpha_a * e^{-i w tau_a} * R(w) with R = F_op - sum_b e^{i w tau_b} K_hat_b; the coherent sum then equals F_op at EVERY frequency by construction. THE KEY INVARIANT to encode and test: sum_{j in C} alpha_j = 1 — this is what makes the reconstruction identity hold. Default switch parameters (rho0, rho1) = (0.5, 4) — keep them as defaults so the ported prototype tests reproduce the paper. DESIGN NOTE the Coder should be aware of but not act on: at the switch-on point w*delta = rho1 = 4 with w=40, a fold has lambda_soft ~ (4/w)^{1/3} ~ 0.46 => p ~ 2 => C1/w ~ 0.17 and C2/w^2 ~ 0.21, i.e. the 'correction' terms are each ~20% — the asymptotic series has barely started. This is a known hazard, documented, NOT to be fixed by retuning the defaults. The `reconstructed`/`reconstruction_error` property pair is reimplemented 4x across the prototype — write it ONCE here (DRY) and have WP6 reuse it. pylint 79 cols.
work_packages.verification: Algebraic-identity unit tests pass with NO lens machinery: on synthetic random (tau_a, K_hat_a, R) inputs the projection reconstructs the target total to ~1e-15; sum alpha_j == 1 to machine precision; smootherstep is C2 (value and first derivative continuous at both x0 and x1, exactly 0 below x0 and exactly 1 above x1). Confirm the module imports without geometry/operator present.

work_packages.title: Topology-stable channels + ChangRefsdalChannels entry point (channels.py)
work_packages.what: The Build-2-facing deliverable: the topology-stable 4-label decomposition F(w) = sum_a e^{i w tau_a} K_a(w) with label continuation, virtual labels at the nearest critical point, the smooth switch, and cluster-local residual projection — exposed through a single entry-point class. Merges the prototype's topology_stable + global_tracking (already coupled); DROPS ~330 lines of validated-but-unused surface.
where: NEW: `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/channels.py`, `cogwheel/tests/test_lensing_channels.py`. EDIT: `cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/__init__.py` (re-export the public API). SOURCE: `chang_refsdal_topology_stable.py` + `chang_refsdal_global_tracking.py`; paper Secs. V-VI + Appendix D.
work_packages.how: SCOPE CUTS — both confirmed by direct code reading, do not port: (1) `chang_refsdal_exact_partition.py` is SUPERSEDED (no test imports it) — drop entirely; this dissolves FoldGeometry/CuspGeometry/FoldPartition/CuspPartition (verbatim duplicate pairs) for free, no collapsing work needed. (2) `build_fold_crossing_partition`/`build_cusp_crossing_partition` (~330 L) plus TopologyStableGeometry/TopologyStablePartition and the privates `_carrier_free_image_kernels`, `_phase_shift_targets`, `_virtual_delays`, `_orient_cusp_basis` are NOT called by `GlobalChannelTracker.evaluate()` — it reimplements its own assignment/switch/projection pipeline inline. They are validated-but-unused production surface: DROP them. Satisfy brief req 1c (fold/cusp continuity) by driving the general tracker along y-paths crossing a fold and a cusp — exactly what the prototype's own `test_global_tracker_exact_on_path_crossing_fold_and_cusp_regions` already does and passes. MANDATORY IMPLEMENTATION-TIME CHECK before deleting: the prototype has FOUR builder-driven single-point tests (`test_fold_fixed_channel_count_and_exactness_both_sides`, `test_channels_are_continuous_at_fold_crossing`, and their cusp siblings) asserting fixed 2-persistent+2-cluster (fold) / 1-persistent+3-cluster (cusp) channel counts and continuity at controlled eta_s/eta_h. Confirm each re-expresses cleanly against `evaluate_path()` output at points straddling the same crossing (the tracker's partition carries the same delays/kernels/real_mask) — if any assertion CANNOT be re-expressed, keep the minimal builder as a TEST HELPER in the test module, never as public API. API (brief hard requirement 3): a single entry-point class `ChangRefsdalChannels` constructed from lens params, exposing vectorized `delays()` -> tau_a (dimensionless, 4 labels ALWAYS), `kernels(w)` -> K_a array, and `amplification(w)` for brute-force reference use. `amplification(w)` MUST be a literal one-line forward into the module-level F_op with self's stored params — it is a bound-instance convenience at a different level, not duplication, PROVIDED it reimplements none of the operator math. Continuation state must support 'evaluate at a nearby parameter point' (path from previous point) AND a deterministic reset convention for far points (paper Appendix D); label_markers/continuation state is API CONTRACT, not diagnostics. Document the label-permutation invariance of the total. THE GEOMETRIC-OPTICS GATE (architect ruling — the brief is technically WRONG here and the Simplifier's 'cut branch' conflated this with the cut asymptotic-1F1 branch): the switch S_j(w*delta_j) governs only the CLUSTER split; G_C = F_op - sum_{p in P} e^{i w tau_p} H_p calls F_op at EVERY frequency, resolved or not. Skipping F_op requires a SEPARATE GLOBAL gate: use_geometric_optics = (w*delta_min >= rho1) AND (L(w,y',gamma') > L_max). Under it K_a := H_a, F_op is never called, and reconstruction is no longer exact — it is O(w^-3), i.e. ~1.6e-5 at w=40 and ~3e-6 at w=80, fine against the paper's 1e-3 interpolation target. The gate MUST be an explicit reported flag `branch` in {'wave','geometric'} on the returned object, and the exact-identity tests MUST be restricted to the wave branch. THIS GATE IS REQUIRED, not optional: one real event spans w by a factor ~51 in band (M_Lz=1e3 => w=2.5 to 127), which runs past the L<=48 wave ceiling, so the engine must be seamless across the gate WITHIN a single waveform. The branches overlap by a wide margin (for a point mass at small y, tau_+ - tau_- ~ 2y so w*delta ~ 2w|y| — the SPA resolution parameter and the series cancellation parameter are THE SAME QUANTITY; the series dies at w|y'| ~ 50 <=> w*delta ~ 100, i.e. 25x past rho1=4). Exploit that overlap — it is test T4. DIAGNOSTICS — adjudicated: keep operator_order_used, operator_converged, estimated_relative_tail, measured max_partial_term/|total| (promoted to runtime refusal), `branch`, and max_stationary_phase_abs (= max_a|H_a|, needed as the reconstruction-test normalizer since H_a is internal). Make n_real_images and active_cluster COMPUTED PROPERTIES derived from real_mask/physical_switch — do not store derived data beside its source. CUT loss_exponent, predicted_digits_lost, spa_condition, max_kernel_abs. Target <= 4 surviving dataclasses total across the subpackage. Reuse WP5's single `reconstructed`/`reconstruction_error` implementation (it is reimplemented 4x in the prototype — do not carry that forward). Rewrite `chang_refsdal_global_tracking.py`'s dense semicolon style to cogwheel idiom. Consult `python scripts/pipeline_graph.py inputs_for cogwheel/lensing/chang_refsdal/channels.py` to confirm no registered data artifact is touched (none expected — no new disk products).

Implements domain tests T4 (geometric-optics w^-3 convergence — the strongest test in the suite), T5 (exact reconstruction as INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, normalized by max(|F_op|, sum|K_a|, max_a|H_a|)), T6b (mass-sheet cross-layer), and T7 (label continuity across fold and cusp + reset convention). All ported prototype assertions hold: exactly 4 labels at every point; reconstruction < 3e-13 on the closed path; all operator_converged. Full subpackage smoke test: construct ChangRefsdalChannels, call delays()/kernels(w)/amplification(w); assert kernels() over a 10-node w-grid <= 20 ms (brief bound: 100 ms).

domain_test_descriptions: T0 — Double-double primitives vs mpmath (WP2). SETUP: adversarial float64 inputs — catastrophic-cancellation pairs (a-b with a~b to within 1 ulp), products spanning many exponents, values near the overflow/underflow rails. OPERATION: each dd primitive (TwoSum, TwoProduct, dd_add/mul/div and their complex forms) compared against mpmath at dps=60. EXPECTED: dd relative error <= 1e-30 wherever mpmath says the result is representable. DIAGNOSTIC: histogram of log10(rel_err) per primitive — should sit near -32 with no tail; a tail means the splitting constant or a renormalization step is wrong. MUST-FAIL CHECK: temporarily perturb the splitting constant from 2^27+1 and confirm the suite goes red — this is the test that catches the silent bug class the Professor flagged.

T1 — Prefactor / Deguchi-Watson exact identity (WP3). SETUP: kappa=gamma=0, y=0, w in logspace(-3, 3, 400). OPERATION: compare |F_op(w, y=0)|^2 against the closed form pi*w/(1 - e^{-pi*w}); separately evaluate F_op(w->0) at y=(0.3,0). EXPECTED: rtol <= 1e-14 at every w and FLAT in w — this is a zero-cancellation identity, so any growth with w is a prefactor bug, not precision loss; and |F_op(1e-5, y=(0.3,0)) - 1| < 1e-4 with the deviation proportional to w as w->0. DIAGNOSTIC: log-log rtol vs w. A flat line at ~1e-15 is correct. A knee at small w means expm1 is missing. A ramp at large w means the e^{pi w/4}*Gamma cancellation was not removed analytically.

T2 — 1F1 ladder vs mpmath oracle, and calibration of the loss law (WP3). SETUP: w in {0.01, 0.1, 1, 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160} x |y'| in {0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.55, 1.0, 2.0} x k in {0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 44, 88, 120}; oracle mpmath.hyp1f1(iw/2, 1+k, iws/2) at dps=60. OPERATION: evaluate the production ladder and compare. EXPECTED: rtol <= 1e-12 wherever w|y'| <= 45; rtol monotonically non-increasing in k at fixed (w,|y'|) (k=0 is the worst case — assert it); and a FIT of log10(rtol) vs w|y'| over the k=0 slice giving slope 0.434 +/- 0.05 with intercept consistent with log10(eps_dd) ~ -32 +/- 1 — fit the law rather than hard-coding its constant, so the test calibrates the domain and survives refactors. Independent cross-check: Miller backward recurrence in k agrees with the ladder to 1e-12 for |z'| >= 5 (test-only; never in the hot path). DIAGNOSTIC: heatmap of log10 rtol over (w, |y'|) with the w|y'| = 45 contour overlaid — the contour must cleanly separate green from red.

T3 — F_op vs mpmath oracle over the paper's configurations (WP4). SETUP: the paper's four Fig.-1 cases at kappa=gamma=0.2, beta=0 — y=(0.55,0) [2-image], y=(0.10,0.10) [4-image], y=(-0.1389,0.1793) [near-fold], y=(-0.395,0) [near-cusp]; w = logspace(-2, 0.7, 20) union linspace(5, 40, 36). Plus two stress cases: oriented shear (kappa=0.27, gamma=0.12, beta=0.31, y=(0.17,-0.08), w=13 — the prototype's own point) and high reduced shear (kappa=0.4, gamma=0.5 => gamma'=0.833, y=(0.3,0.1), w in {10,20,40}). Oracle: mpmath at dps=80, max_order=60, series tolerance 1e-20. OPERATION: evaluate production F_op and compare. EXPECTED: rtol <= 1e-10 at every point with L <= 48 (all the above qualify — the headline y=0.55 at w=40 is L=29.6); report measured rtol vs L and assert consistency with the law fitted in T2. DIAGNOSTIC: per configuration, three stacked panels vs w — |F_op|, unwrapped arg F_op, and log10 rtol. rtol should sit at 1e-13..1e-15 and rise only where L does.

T4 — Geometric-optics limit; the single strongest test in the suite (WP6). SETUP: kappa=gamma=0.2, beta=0, y=(0.55,0), w in {10, 14, 20, 28, 40, 56, 80} (geometric ladder). OPERATION: Delta(w) = |F_op(w) - sum_a e^{i w tau_a} H_a(w)| / |F_op(w)| using tau_a and H_a from the quartic geometry and the Appendix-B C1/C2 coefficients; repeat with C2=0, and with C1=C2=0. EXPECTED: fitting log Delta vs log w over w in [20,80] gives slope -3.0 +/- 0.3 with both coefficients, -2.0 +/- 0.3 with C2=0, and -1.0 +/- 0.3 with both zeroed; absolute Delta(40) < 3e-4, Delta(80) < 5e-5. DIAGNOSTIC: log-log Delta vs w with reference slopes -1, -2, -3 drawn. WHY IT MATTERS: this is the only test that couples the operator, the prefactor normalization, the quartic geometry, the signed magnifications, the Morse indices and the C1/C2 polynomials through a channel with NO shared code — a sign error in C1, a wrong Morse index e^{-i pi n/2}, a factor-of-2 in w, or a wrong C(w) normalization each produces a distinct, unmistakable slope failure.

T5 — Exact reconstruction, as INTERNAL CONSISTENCY (WP6). SETUP: the paper's fold and cusp crossings, eta in linspace(-0.02, 0.02, 41), w in linspace(5, 40, 71), wave branch only. OPERATION: r = |sum_a e^{i w tau_a} K_a - F_op|; also record min_a|K_a|, max_a|H_a|; also permute the label order and recompute the sum. EXPECTED: r <= 1e-13 * max(|F_op|, sum_a|K_a|, max_a|H_a|) at every (eta, w) — NORMALIZED BY THE LARGEST INTERMEDIATE, NOT BY |F_op|, because |H_a| ~ lambda_soft^-6.5 near critical curves and a |F_op|-relative 1e-12 would fail there and get 'fixed' by loosening something real; exactly 4 labels defined at every point; min_a|K_a| >= 0.4 (paper: 0.47 cusp / 0.59 fold); label-permutation invariance of the total to 1e-15. THE TEST DOCSTRING MUST STATE: 'F_op appears on both sides of this identity; this verifies the projection algebra and the weight normalization sum_{j in C} alpha_j = 1, NOT the accuracy of F_op — accuracy is T3/T4.' DIAGNOSTIC: log10(r/normalizer) heatmap over (eta, w) with a companion panel of max_a|H_a| — the two must track each other where r rises.

T6 — Mass-sheet identity, in three non-vacuous parts plus one labelled tautology (WP4/WP6). SETUP: kappa in {0.1, 0.27, 0.4, 0.5}, gamma=0.12, beta=0.31, y=(0.17,-0.08); plus a 4-image case y=(0.02,0.01). (a) GEOMETRY — genuinely independent, since the quartic at A(kappa,gamma,beta) and the quartic at A(gamma',beta,0) are different polynomials: images from A(kappa,gamma,beta) vs lambda^{-1/2} x images from the kappa=0 problem at y/sqrt(lambda) — same count, position match < 1e-10, delays satisfying tau_kappa(x;y) = tau_{0,gamma'}(x';y') + 0.5*ln(lambda) - kappa|y|^2/(2 lambda) to 1e-13 absolute, mu_kappa = mu'/lambda^2 to 1e-12 relative, lens residual < 1e-11. (b) CROSS-LAYER: |F_op(kappa,gamma,beta,y) - sum_a e^{i w tau_a} H_a| / |F_op| < 1e-4 at w=60, exhibiting T4's w^-3 slope. (c) ZERO-LIMIT — tests the whole normalization chain (prefactor, mass-sheet, operator series) in one number: |F_op(w->0) * sqrt((1-kappa)^2 - gamma^2) - 1| < 1e-3 at w=1e-4. (d) GUARD, EXPLICITLY DOCUMENTED AS A TAUTOLOGY: the prototype's LHS-vs-externally-mapped-RHS check at tol 1e-15, with the docstring 'both sides evaluate the identical series with identical arguments; this asserts only that the prefactor algebra is written once. The shipped prototype's 2e-12 threshold on this comparison is not meaningful.' DIAGNOSTIC: scatter of delay-identity residual vs kappa; must be flat, not growing with kappa.

T7 — Label continuity across fold and cusp, and the reset convention (WP6). SETUP: a continuation path varying y, gamma, beta through 2- and 4-image regions (>= 49 points, >= 4 changes in image count — e.g. the prototype's closed path y = 0.18*(cos t, 0.75 sin t)), w grid linspace(5, 40, 10). OPERATION: per label a, form path-differences of tau_a and of ln K_a(w); then call reset_labels() at an arbitrary path point. EXPECTED: (i) exactly 4 labels defined at every point INCLUDING where the image count changes; (ii) no path-step in tau_a, |K_a| or arg K_a exceeds 5x the median step for that label — a refactor-proof statement of 'no permutation swap'; do NOT assert on absolute positions, which are only ~1e-8 accurate near caustics; (iii) T5's reconstruction holds at every path point; (iv) reset_labels() reproduces, UP TO A PERMUTATION, the same set of (tau_a, K_a) — asserting the reset convention agrees with continuation on the SET, not the ordering. DIAGNOSTIC: 4-curve overlays of |K_a| and unwrapped arg K_a vs path index (no crossings, no jumps), plus lens-plane marker tracks with the caustic overlaid — virtual labels must sit on the critical curve.

T8 — Quartic geometry vs the shipped validation CSV, and performance (WP1/WP4/WP6). SETUP: `.claude/spec/lensing_paper/data/quartic_geometry_validation.csv` (168 rows; columns index, kind, gamma, beta, y1, y2, n_quartic, n_multistart, matched_position_error, max_quartic_residual; covers 'general' random draws up to gamma~0.62 and a structured 'cusp' scan straddling y2 = sqrt(2) where the image count drops 4->2). OPERATION: re-run the production quartic solver on every row. EXPECTED: n_quartic == n_multistart in 168/168; max_quartic_residual <= 1e-12 (CSV shows ~1e-14 typical, paper max 1.8e-13); matched_position_error <= 3e-12 (paper: 2.1e-12); for rows within 1e-5 of a caustic assert on RESIDUAL AND DELAY, not on position. PERF (same module, after warm-up): single F_op <= 2 ms at kappa=gamma=0.2, y=(0.55,0), w=20 (target <= 200 us, brief bound 10 ms); channels.kernels() over a 10-node w-grid <= 20 ms (brief bound 100 ms); operator_order_used <= 25 at gamma'=0.25, w=40, guarding against adaptive truncation silently running to max_order. STRUCTURAL: assert the production import graph contains no reference to mpmath — timing alone will not catch a 10-node mpmath path on a fast machine. DIAGNOSTIC: histogram of lens-equation residuals; scatter of residual vs distance-to-caustic, which must not grow faster than d^{-1/2}. NOTE: this is the one test that reads a data file — an exception the brief explicitly grants (req 1e) against cogwheel's convention that tests synthesize their inputs in-process; do not generalize it into a fixture-shipping pattern.
simplifier_inputs: DEPENDENCY GRAPH CORRECTION (reshaped the whole WP order): the brief's file list implies a sequence that the actual imports contradict. geometry.py, operator.py and exact_gauge_partition.py are ALL leaves — operator does NOT import geometry. So WP1 (geometry) and WP5 (channel algebra) run fully in parallel with WP2->WP3->WP4, and only WP6 needs the joins. Scoping WP6 off the brief's file list rather than the dependency graph was called out as the plan's single biggest structural risk.

DROP chang_refsdal_exact_partition.py entirely (superseded, no test imports it). This dissolves the '9-dataclass sprawl' for free: FoldGeometry==CuspGeometry and FoldPartition==CuspPartition are verbatim duplicates that live ONLY in that dead file, and 3 of the 4 reimplementations of reconstructed/reconstruction_error go with it. No collapsing work needed — just don't port it. Target <=4 surviving dataclasses.

DROP build_fold_crossing_partition / build_cusp_crossing_partition (~330 L + 2 dataclasses + 4 privates): verified by reading both bodies that GlobalChannelTracker.evaluate() never calls them — it reimplements assignment/switch/projection inline. They are validated-but-unused production surface that grew production-shaped return types. The prototype's own path test already drives evaluate_path() along a fold/cusp-crossing closed path asserting reconstruction < 3e-13, which is exactly the mechanism brief req 1c needs. CAVEAT CARRIED INTO WP6: four builder-driven single-point tests must be confirmed re-expressible against evaluate_path() before deletion; if any can't be, keep a minimal builder as a TEST HELPER only.

KEEP the channel algebra (exact_gauge_partition.py) as its own leaf module rather than merging it into channels.py as the brief's file list implies — it has zero geometry/operator dependency and is testable as pure algebraic identities; burying it inside the heaviest, most stateful WP would block it behind WP1+WP4 for no complexity benefit. Split channels.py's SOURCES by dependency, not by the brief's file list. (topology_stable + global_tracking merging IS fine — they're already coupled.)

DOUBLE-DOUBLE IS 'WATCH — JUSTIFIED', and the deferral options were explicitly rejected. Shipping Build 1 capped at L<=12-15 'isn't a smaller deliverable, it's an incomplete one wearing a passing test suite' — the test would pass by gerrymandering the domain around a known weakness, the same anti-pattern as a test that can't fail. Deferring dd to Build 2 costs MORE (retrofitting into an already-integrated kernel whose shape and perf Build 2 depends on) and blocks Build 2 outright rather than deferring independent work, since Build 2's own w range (2.5-127 in band) runs straight through the region where plain double is known-wrong.

_dd.py MUST be its own module AND its own WP, gated before WP3 starts. A generic numerical primitive with zero coupling to hypergeometric logic, independently testable against mpmath. The decisive argument: if a combined WP2 fails its oracle test, a Coder burning turns on 'is this the dd primitives or the series algorithm?' is close to the worst version of turn exhaustion — the debugging, not the implementation, eats the budget. A wrong TwoProduct constant would masquerade as a hypergeometric bug.

ALL FOUR Professor cuts confirmed against the prototype code, and three are correctness fixes rather than mere simplifications: no large-|z| asymptotic branch (dead code, and the brief already hedged it with 'if needed'); no k-recurrence (the prototype ALREADY only varies b=1+k across the ladder, so the shared-t_m factorization is a straight upgrade with no downside); closed-form |C(w)| (verified |Gamma(1-iw/2)| = sqrt(pi(w/2)/sinh(pi w/2)) — removes a real overflow/underflow dance, not an exp() count); and beta-rotation (the lru_cache is keyed on a CONTINUOUS float, so along any PE path it essentially never hits after the first call — dead weight that LOOKS like an optimization, corroborated independently by the memory's 'never sample beta'). Reject the 'cuts pay for dd' accounting framing though: dd is justified on its own merits, and the cuts' real payoff is RISK REDUCTION — they remove three other places where subtle numerical bugs could compound with dd's bug surface and make a failing oracle test harder to root-cause.

DIAGNOSTICS HAD OUTGROWN THEIR PURPOSE — 'log everything conceivable' rather than 'what a consumer needs to trust or debug the result'. Cut loss_exponent and predicted_digits_lost (they are the analytic prediction the Professor's own argument says is LESS trustworthy than the measured value — shipping both invites trusting the wrong one), spa_condition, and max_kernel_abs (a one-line np.max — a field that adds no logic). Reclassify n_real_images/active_cluster as computed properties (storing derived data beside its source is a DRY violation waiting to go stale) and label_markers as API contract, not reporting. PROMOTE the measured max_partial_term/|total| from a passive field to a RUNTIME REFUSAL: 'a safety mechanism nobody is required to look at isn't a safety mechanism'.

mpmath: add a `test` extra with NO skipUnless guard. A skip on an accuracy gate — the brief's own words, 'the build gate' — is actively dangerous: it lets the single most important correctness test silently vanish in exactly the environment (missing optional dep) where you'd most want it to fail loud. The repo's existing optional-heavy-dependency pattern (pymultinest under `full`) is to fail loudly with an ImportError at point of use, not to skip. And a shipped mpmath-generated oracle fixture would invent a new committed data artifact (with DATA_CONTRACTS bookkeeping) purely to dodge an oracle-only dependency — more moving parts, not fewer. The one CSV read is pre-existing manuscript data the brief itself mandates: an exception already granted, not one to generalize.

ChangRefsdalChannels.amplification(w) alongside a module-level F_op is NOT duplication — they sit at different levels (F_op is the stateless primitive needed anyway by the oracle tests and used internally by channels.py). But it comes with a hard constraint: it must be a literal one-line forward with self's stored params. If the method reimplements any operator math, THAT is the violation to catch in review — not the existence of two entry points.

ARCHITECT OVERRULED the Simplifier on two points, both recorded for the Inspector. (1) The `branch` ('wave'|'geometric') gate: the Simplifier voted cut, but conflated it with the (correctly cut) asymptotic-1F1 branch. They are different — the gate skips F_op ENTIRELY in geometric optics, is required because in-band w reaches 127+ past the L<=48 wave ceiling within a single waveform, and is demanded by brief req 2. (2) dd scope: the Simplifier's dd-seed-only fallback was checked against the headline config and passes there (gamma'w/2 = 5 <= 8), but gamma'=0.9 at w=40 gives 18, and gamma'->1 is the astrophysically interesting high-magnification limit; with 10-200x perf headroom, one arithmetic mode throughout is simpler than two.
